playDescription: The through-ball is played from the left and the attacker runs onto it near the penalty arc. The camera is panning and the second-to-last defender is partially out of frame at the decisive moment, so the relative positions of attacker and defender at the instant of the pass cannot be established with confidence.
reasoning: A definitive offside judgement requires a clear view of both the attacker and the second-to-last defender at the exact frame the ball is played. This single broadcast angle does not provide that — the defender leaves frame and there is motion blur across the key frame — so neither a fair nor a bad call can be supported. A calibrated offside line or a second angle would be needed.

rulesCited.title: Offside offence — moment of judgement
rulesCited.text: The offside position is assessed at the moment the ball is played or touched by a teammate, not at the moment the ball is received.
